nodes.name: Replicated log
nodes.statement: Raft keeps a log of client commands on every server. Each server applies those commands in log order to its own state machine.

nodes.name: Deterministic state machines
nodes.statement: A deterministic state machine that starts in the same state and applies the same commands in the same order always ends in the same state.

nodes.name: One vote per term
nodes.statement: Raft numbers its elections by term. Each server votes for at most one candidate per term and saves that vote to disk before replying.

nodes.name: Majority size
nodes.statement: A majority of n servers means more than n/2 of them, so a cluster of 5 needs 3 and a cluster of 4 also needs 3.

nodes.name: Majorities overlap
nodes.statement: Any two majorities of the same cluster share at least one server, because together they count more than n servers.

nodes.name: Winning an election
nodes.statement: A candidate becomes leader only after it collects votes from a majority of the cluster.

nodes.name: Election Safety
nodes.statement: At most one leader can be elected in any given term.

nodes.name: Election timeout
nodes.statement: A follower that hears no heartbeat from a leader within its election timeout becomes a candidate and starts a new term.

nodes.name: Randomized timeouts
nodes.statement: Each server picks its election timeout at random from a fixed range, such as 150 to 300 milliseconds.

nodes.name: Split votes are rare
nodes.statement: With random timeouts, one server usually times out first and wins before others start competing. So split votes are rare, and the few that happen end after one more timeout.

nodes.name: Stable leadership
nodes.statement: In a healthy cluster, Raft usually elects a leader within a few hundred milliseconds. It keeps that leader as long as the leader's heartbeats arrive in time.

nodes.name: Stepping down
nodes.statement: A server that sees a message carrying a higher term than its own adopts that term. If it was a leader or candidate, it becomes a follower.

nodes.name: Leader Append-Only
nodes.statement: A leader never overwrites or deletes entries in its own log. It only appends new ones.

nodes.name: AppendEntries check
nodes.statement: Each AppendEntries message carries the index and term of the entry just before the new ones. A follower rejects the message if its log has no matching entry at that spot.

nodes.name: One entry per index
nodes.statement: In any given term, a leader creates at most one entry at each log index.

nodes.name: Log Matching
nodes.statement: If two logs contain an entry with the same index and term, the logs are identical in every entry up to that index.

nodes.name: Follower log repair
nodes.statement: When the consistency check fails, the leader retries with earlier entries until it finds the last point where both logs agree. It then overwrites the follower's conflicting entries with its own.

nodes.name: Commit rule
nodes.statement: An entry is committed once the leader that created it has stored it on a majority of servers.

nodes.name: Voting restriction
nodes.statement: A server refuses to vote for a candidate whose log is less up to date than its own. Logs are compared by the term of the last entry first and then by length.

nodes.name: Leader Completeness
nodes.statement: A leader elected in any term already holds every entry committed in earlier terms.

nodes.name: Old-term entries hazard
nodes.statement: An entry from an earlier term can be stored on a majority of servers and still be overwritten by a later leader.

nodes.name: Counting current-term replicas
nodes.statement: A Raft leader commits an entry by counting replicas only when the entry is from its own current term. Older entries then become committed along with it, because of Log Matching.

nodes.name: Apply only committed
nodes.statement: A server applies an entry to its state machine only after it learns that the entry is committed.

nodes.name: State Machine Safety
nodes.statement: If a server has applied a log entry at a given index, no other server will ever apply a different entry at that index.

nodes.name: Replicas agree
nodes.statement: Every server that applies the log passes through the same sequence of states.

nodes.name: Fault tolerance
nodes.statement: A cluster of 2f + 1 servers can still elect a leader and commit entries while up to f servers are down.

nodes.name: Five-server cluster
nodes.statement: A five-server Raft cluster keeps working with two servers down, because the three remaining servers still form a majority.

nodes.name: Deposed leader is harmless
nodes.statement: A deposed leader from an older term cannot commit new entries. The servers that elected the new leader have moved to a higher term and reject its messages, and any majority it needs includes one of them.

nodes.name: Durable acknowledgement
nodes.statement: A Raft leader reports a command as successful only after its entry is committed. So an acknowledged command survives every later change of leader.
